introduction.en: Money supply refers to the total stock of money circulating in an economy at a given point in time. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) classifies this into various measures based on liquidity.
introduction.hi: Money supply refers to the total stock of money circulating in an economy at a given point in time. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) classifies this into various measures based on liquidity.

body.en: The measures include M0 (Reserve Money), M1 (Narrow Money), M2, M3 (Broad Money), and M4. M1 is highly liquid, while M3 is the most widely used measure for policy as it captures the total monetary resources. RBI uses these aggregates to manage inflation and liquidity in the banking system.

conclusion.en: Understanding these measures is crucial for the RBI to maintain price stability and support economic growth.
